blocks.html: If these witnesses had not been singular, each deposing to his own fact, and well objected to, this proof alone would indeed have been sufficient to put him to the torture [géhenne]. For although a confession of a crime, made out of judgment, is not sufficient to condemn a man, without a new trial, or else extraordinarily at the discretion of the Judge, as a fool, vainglorious and overweening, having boasted of doing ill a: nevertheless it makes a sufficient indication for putting such a rustic, who has confessed, to the torture b.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 5.31.9 (De excessibus praelatorum et subditorum, c. Quam sit grave)
notes.original: c. quàm ſit graue. de ex. ceſ. prelato
notes.gloss: Cited for the rule that a confession made out of court does not of itself convict, but may draw an extraordinary penalty on the boaster; the print's prelato has a plain e for praelato.

notes.citation: Accursius (Accurſe), the Gloss on Digest 48.5.26 (old numbering 48.5.25) (Ad legem Iuliam de adulteriis coercendis, l. Capite quinto; Ulpian)
notes.original: Accurſe en la l. capite quinto- D. de adult,
notes.gloss: The extrajudicial confession as an indicium sufficient for torture.
